route_markers.label: Climb — Cat 1
route_markers.name: Alto de la Venta de la Cebada

guideposts.label: Welcome to Granada
guideposts.detail: Today's stage is entirely set in the province of Granada, a staple of La Vuelta and particularly of the 2026 edition. Granada was a stage town already in the first La Vuelta (1935). It has hosted the Gran Salida in 2005 and 2008. Next week-end, it will host the finale for the first time in the history of the Spanish Grand Tour. The last stage winner in the province of Granada is Adam Yates, in 202

guideposts.label: On Carlos Rodriguez’s roads
guideposts.detail: Almuñécar make its debut as La Vuelta stage town*. It is the hometown of Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos), who was born here on 2 February 2001. The Spanish climber is taking part in La Vuelta for the third time. In 2022, he wore Spain’s national champion and finished 6th overall. In 2024, he was 10th. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Felix Gall, Gregor Mühlberger and Léo Bisiaux at the front, Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance yesterday and extended their lead in the overall team standings. Bahrain Victorious are now second (+1h06’11’’) ahead of Netcompany Ineos (+1h06’31’’).

guideposts.label: First attacks
guideposts.detail: Four riders currently lead the way but the battle rages on.

guideposts.label: Flying past Salobreña
guideposts.detail: Next to Almuñécar, Salobreña (km 5 on today’s route) hosted the start of stage 12 of La Vuelta 22. Richard Carapaz won at Peñas Blanca, where Remco Evenepoel retained La Roja ahead of Primoz Roglic and Enric Mas. Marco Brenner (5th), José Manuel Diaz (12th), Alexey Lutsenko (26th), Carlos Canal (28th) and Ivo Oliveira (77th) were part of the breakaway with Carapaz.

guideposts.label: The gap slightly increases: 40'' at km 12
guideposts.detail: The road will soon rise for the cat. 1 ascent of the day, the Alto de la Venta de la Cebada (14.1 km at 5.1%, with gradients up to 12%). The foot is at km 17.1.

guideposts.label: Berrade is caught by the bunch
guideposts.detail: The four leaders are 50'' away

guideposts.label: A gap of 32'' at km 21
guideposts.detail: The battle goes on with ten kilometres left on the first climb of the day.

guideposts.label: The gap drops down to 12 seconds
guideposts.detail: Will the early attackers get caught or will they receive some support to pull away again?

guideposts.label: Fortunato on the move
guideposts.detail: Lorenzo Fortunato is the XDS Astana rider who has opened a small gap to the bunch.

guideposts.label: Kron joins Fortunato at the front
guideposts.detail: Among the most active riders to make the breakaways in this edition of La Vuelta, Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) said at the start he wants to make the most of today's opportunity.

guideposts.label: The bunch splits in two after a crash
guideposts.detail: Radio Vuelta reports Gregor Mühlberger (Decathlon CMA CGM) has hit the deck, and that he has resumed racing.

guideposts.label: Albanese bridges the gap to make it a 28-man front group
guideposts.detail: The peloton trail by 20 seconds.

guideposts.label: Van Aert attacks from the front group
guideposts.detail: Fortunato is with him, a few metres ahead of the rest of the attackers.

guideposts.label: Muhlberger abandons
guideposts.detail: Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) loses a key teammate for the mountains.

guideposts.label: More attackers, including Skjelmose
guideposts.detail: Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious), Mattias Skjlemose (Lidl-Trek), Jan Hirt (NSN), Magnus Cort, Simon Dalby, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Sylvain Moniquet, Sergio Samitier (Cofidis), Will Barta (Tudor), Mario Aparicio (Burgos Burpellet BH), Jarno Widar, Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) and Iñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) have joined the breakaway. The peloton

guideposts.label: The battle goes on
guideposts.detail: Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana) and Iñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) attack from the breakaway. At km 51, the chasers are 17 seconds ahead of the chasers. The peloton trail by 1'23''.

guideposts.label: 3 leaders, 2 chase groups
guideposts.detail: Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana) and Iñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) keep going. +12'' Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos), Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious), Rudy Molard (Groupama-FDJ United), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) +20'' The rest of the attackers +1'57'' Peloton

guideposts.label: 10 leaders
guideposts.detail: Vermaerke, Brennan, Laurance, Miquel, Molard, Paret-Peintre, Kron, Albanese, Cr. Rodriguez and Elosegui are now 20 seconds ahead of their rivals.

guideposts.label: Attacks keep flying at the front
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, the gap to the bunch increases: 2'40''.

guideposts.label: A new lead trio
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) are riding 20 seconds ahead of the chase group.

guideposts.label: 3 minutes
guideposts.detail: While the battle rages on at the front, the gap to the bunch steadily increases.

guideposts.label: More attacks
guideposts.detail: Now it's a 6-man group leading the way with Vermaerke, Brennan, Laurance...

guideposts.label: The situation at km 70
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos), Clément Berthet, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Andreas Kron, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Vincenzo Albanese (EF Education-EasyPost), and Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana) lead the way. +40’’ Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) +1’05’’ Chase group +3'35'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Bisiaux and Craps join the front group
guideposts.detail: That makes 11 leaders on the ascent of the Alto del Legionario.

guideposts.label: 3 abandons today
guideposts.detail: In addition to Gregor Mühlberger (Decathlon CMA CGM), Francesco Busatto and Sente Sentjens (Alpecin-Premier Tech) also left the race.

guideposts.label: Sivakov also abandons
guideposts.detail: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG) called for the medical car earlier in the stage.

guideposts.label: Results at the Alto del Legionario (cat. 2, km 83.4)
guideposts.detail: 1. Albanese, 5 pts 2. Martin-Guyonnet, 3 pts 3. Kron, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Into the final 100 kilometres
guideposts.detail: The eleven leaders keep pushing. Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos) just went down in a turn. He rapidly got back up. The chasers trail by a minute. The gap to the peloton has increased to four minutes.

guideposts.label: De la Cruz has crashed in the chase group
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard suffers from his right shoulder but he gets back up and resumes racing. Axel Laurance is also back in action after his crash.

guideposts.label: De la Cruz is caught by the bunch
guideposts.detail: Movistar and EF Education-EasyPost work together to control the gap. They are 4 minutes behind the leaders, and two and a half minutes behind the Skjelmose group.

guideposts.label: 80 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The ten leaders are 1'20'' ahead of the peloton, while the peloton control the gap at 4 minutes. The riders are on a flat section leading to the intermediate sprint (Tocon, km 145) and then the final climb of the day, Puerto de Granada (cat. 2, summit at km 155.4).

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 40.8 km/h
guideposts.detail: The pace has been really demanding with the heat and the many hills.

guideposts.label: Gearing to make history in Loja
guideposts.detail: Loja is a La Vuelta stage town for the second time after hosting the start on day 6 of the 1990 edition - so it will be the first finish here. The race headed to Ubrique, where Jesper Worre tooth win and Julian Gorospe claimed the overall lead. Also part of the day’s breakaway, Italy’s Marco Giovannetti gained four minutes on the peloton and eventually won La Vuelta a couple of weeks later in Madr

guideposts.label: 60 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), Clément Berthet, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Andreas Kron, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Vincenzo Albanese (EF Education-EasyPost), Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana), and Lars Craps (Lotto Intermarché) have increased their lead: +1'30'' Chase group +4'40'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Martin-Guyonnet helps Berthet move up in the overall standings
guideposts.detail: Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United) is known for his ability to gain time and places in the overall standings through long range attacks. Today, he's setting the pace at the front for Clément Berthet, who started the day 11th and is already set to enter the GC top 10 after Gregor Mühlberger (Decathlon CMA CGM) crashed out of the race. "I hope I’ll have opportunities to pick up some tim

guideposts.label: De Pestel has crashed
guideposts.detail: Felix Gall's Belgian teammate got back on his bike.

guideposts.label: Into the final 50 kilometres
guideposts.detail: The situation has settled ahead of the intermediate sprint and the final climb.

guideposts.label: Vermaerke attacks 2.5 km from the summit
guideposts.detail: Brennan is the quickest to react. Leknessund counter-attacks. Martin-Guyonnet and Albanese struggle.

guideposts.label: Van Aert increases the pace
guideposts.detail: Albanese is caught.

guideposts.label: Vermaerke attacks over the top
guideposts.detail: A dozen chasers bridged the gap just before the summit.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 4 hours: 40.8 km/h
guideposts.detail: The battle rages on: chasers are moving closer to the leaders, while the peloton trail by 4'20''.

guideposts.label: The chasers catch the leaders
guideposts.detail: 28 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: 9 leaders with 25 km to go
guideposts.detail: Fisher-Black, Vermaerke, Van Aert, Brennan, Bisiaux, Paret-Peintre, Dalby, Albanese and Widar have opened a gap.

guideposts.label: Van Aert attacks
guideposts.detail: Vermaerke and Paret-Peintre follow. Albanese chases with Brennan and the other attackers on his wheel. With 23 km to go, they are 25 seconds ahead of the chase group.

guideposts.label: 20 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The leaders get back together and the chasers lose time: 55 seconds.

guideposts.label: Vermaerke attacks...
guideposts.detail: Van Aert follows; Fisher-Black bridges the gap; Albanese brings back the rest of the group.

guideposts.label: Bisiaux tries with 7 km to go
guideposts.detail: Fisher-Black is the quickest to react, followed by Brennan and the rest of the group. With these dynamics, the gaps decrease: 45'' for the chasers, 3'55'' for the peloton.

guideposts.label: Van Aert puts the hammer down with 3.5 km to go
guideposts.detail: Paret-Peintre is on his wheel but it's hard!

guideposts.label: Van Aert and Paret-Peintre have opened a gap
guideposts.detail: They are 2 kilometres from the finish.

guideposts.label: Wout van Aert wins stage 13 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: His first victory in this edition after he claimed three in 2024!

guideposts.label: Brennan finishes 3rd
guideposts.detail: 1. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) 3. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), +24'' 4. Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) 5. Vincenzo Albanese (EF Education-EasyPost)

guideposts.label: Skjelmose gains 2'10''
guideposts.detail: The Dane finished with a gap of 50'' while a reduced bunch crossed the line 3 minutes after Van Aert.
